Subject: Advance-commit (multi-year) — entity & tax routing questions

Alex / Laura —

Thanks for the fast demo last week. We are internally aligned to move forward with a multi-year advance commitment (3 years) but have a few billing/tax items procurement needs cleared before we can sign. High level questions below — can your team confirm options and any limitations?

1) Invoice currency / FX risk: We prefer an annual EUR invoice (our treasury manages FX centrally). Can Redwood invoice in EUR from an EU entity, or would we receive USD invoices from Redwood, which we would then convert? If Redwood can invoice in EUR, please confirm the invoicing entity and VAT handling.

2) VAT / reverse charge: As an EU B2B purchase, we typically handle reverse-charge VAT. Can Redwood issue an invoice without VAT and include your VAT ID so we can self-account? If not, what evidence/registration do you need?

3) Withholding tax (WHT): Our legal/finance ask whether there are any cross-border withholding implications if Redwood invoices from a US entity. If WHT applies, do you gross up or will that reduce the net we pay? We may have treaty relief — need the line items on the stub.

4) Contract entity / invoicing split: For a large prepay we sometimes request a split invoice schedule (Year 1 upfront, Years 2–3 annual prepayments) or a single up-front charge with scheduled recognition. Does Redwood support both models and any pricing impact for splitting?

5) Discount / ramp schedule: We expect a ramped usage profile (low in Y1, higher in Y2–Y3). Are term discounts tied to commitment dollars or to expected consumption? Example ask: can we do a 3-year advance with 15% term discount and a year-by-year ramp schedule (10% Y1, 15% Y2, 20% Y3) — is that modeled?

If it helps, we can share our standard PO terms. Also please include an example invoice stub and the tax doc we would need to push through Treasury.

Appreciate a quick runbook — our QBR is next week and procurement would like to confirm the approach by 6/4.

Thanks,
Nate Turner

Nate — thanks for the clear list. Putting options below so your procurement and treasury can pick the path that fits your controls. I copied Laura (finance) and Dev (legal/contracts) for the details.

Short answers up front:
- Invoice currency: We can invoice in EUR from our EU billing entity (Redwood Inference EU SARL) for customers registered in the EU. If you prefer USD, we can invoice from Redwood, Inc. (US).
- VAT: For B2B EU customers with a valid VAT ID, we support reverse-charge invoices (no VAT charged) from the EU entity. We need your VAT number on the PO and the billing contact.
- WHT: If invoiced from the US entity, certain countries may consider supplier income subject to withholding. We do not generally gross-up. However, if you provide treaty documentation (and we provide the required US tax forms), we can arrange to document the reduced WHT.
- Split vs single prepay: We can support a single up-front prepay or a staged/annual prepay schedule. Pricing differences are primarily timing of cash receipt — term discounts are based on committed dollars (not actual consumption), so you can structure tiered discounts on the commitment schedule.

Attached: a sample 3-year advance-commit invoice stub in EUR and a short tax note with the common Redwood forms we can provide.

Proposed commercial approach (flexible):
- Option A (single upfront): 3-year advance, invoice in EUR from EU entity, term discount 17% on list ARR, no VAT charged (reverse-charge). Yearly reconciliation for consumption vs commitment.
- Option B (staged): Year 1 prepaid (invoice in EUR), Year 2 & 3 invoiced annually in advance at agreed schedule — term discount applied on total committed dollars (example schedule below).

Example ramp schedule for modeling:
- Committed dollars total: EUR 900k over 3 years (300k year-equivalent)
- Year 1 consumption expected 40% of committed run-rate -> we can apply a 12% effective discount in Y1 for lower utilization and step up to 17% in Y2 and 20% in Y3 tied to committed dollars being still in place. This is a commercial construct we can operationalize in the invoice and recognition schedule; legal will need the final language on payment schedule and termination pro-ration.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm invoicing entity preference (EU entity vs US entity + EUR vs USD).
2) If EU entity + reverse-charge, send VAT number and PO details.
3) Dev/Legal will prepare a short addendum capturing split vs single prepay and discount tiers.
4) We will send a DocuSign-ready contract + invoice stub once you confirm.

Laura / Dev — anything to add on documentation needed for WHT relief?

Best,

Hi Nate — quick finance note to make Treasury’s life easier.

1) If you invoice us (sorry — the other way around): when Redwood issues invoices from the EU entity and you self-account via reverse-charge, we need the following on the PO/invoice: your company legal name, EU VAT number, billing address, and the statement "reverse charge applies — Article 194" (or local equivalent).

2) If Redwood invoices from the US entity and you apply withholding: please include the gross amount, the WHT rate and the net amount on your remittance. We will provide the appropriate US forms depending on entity type (W-8BEN-E or W-8ECI). We do not typically gross-up the invoice — the contract will reflect that withholding is a payer responsibility and amounts will be net of withholding unless the parties explicitly agree to gross-up.

3) Documents attached: Redwood_W9_W8_WHT_note.pdf (explains which forms we provide and examples of treaty lines), and a sample invoice stub (Redwood_AdvanceCommit_3yr_EUR_stub.pdf) that shows the line items for term discount and gross/net breakdown for WHT scenarios.

If you confirm EU entity invoicing and send your VAT number, we can generate a final invoice and DocuSign package today.

Regards,
